Application Materials.content:
For international students, as part of the application process, you'll need to submit:
- School or college transcripts/certificates
- University transcripts and certified translations if applicable
- Degree certificates
- Evidence of English Language proficiency (unless you're a national of a [majority English speaking country](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/international/applying/entry-requirements/english-language-requirements/majority-english-speaking-countries/))
- Personal statement outlining your learning ambitions.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **Postgraduate entry requirements:** We accept a **2:2 honours degree** from a UK university, or an equivalent academic qualification from a similar non-UK institution. This degree should be **in a relevant subject**.
- Non-graduates with **very extensive professional experience and/or other prior qualifications** may also be considered.
- **China (mainland) international qualifications:** Taught master's applications with a bachelor's degree from a **recognised Chinese university**, with overall average academic grades between **65% to 78%** depending on the level/tier of Chinese university, will generally be considered for admissions onto taught master's programmes. Some courses do require higher entry requirements; see individual course pages for full details.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
You'll need to demonstrate competence in the use of English language, unless you’re from a [majority English speaking country](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/international/applying/entry-requirements/english-language-requirements/majority-english-speaking-countries/). We accept a variety of [international language tests](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/international/applying/entry-requirements/english-language-requirements/international-english-language-tests/) and [country-specific qualifications](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/international/applying/entry-requirements/english-language-requirements/country-specific-qualifications/). International applicants who do not meet the minimum required standard of English language can complete one of our [Pre-Sessional English courses](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/courses/data-science-and-analytics-for-society-msc#pre-sessional-english) to achieve the required level.
| Qualification | Details |
| --- | --- |
| IELTS | **6.5 overall, with no component below 5.5** |
| TOEFL iBT | If you took a TOEFL test on or before 20 January 2026, you’ll need **88 overall**, with minimum scores of listening 17, writing 17, reading 17 and speaking 19. If you took a TOEFL test from 21 January 2026 onwards, when a new scoring system was introduced, you’ll need **4.5 overall**, with 4 or above in all components. TOEFL Home Edition not accepted. |
| Duolingo English Test | **125 overall**, with speaking, reading and writing not less than 105, and listening not below 100. For academic year 2025/26 only, we will also accept the production, literacy, comprehension and conversation score set: **120 overall**, with no component below 95. |
| Pearson PTE Academic | **61 overall, with no component below 59** |
| LanguageCert Academic | **70 overall, with no skill below 60** |
| PSI Skills for English | **B2 Pass with Merit overall and no band below B2 Pass** |
| INDIA Standard XII | National Curriculum (CBSE/ISC) - **75% and above in English**. Accepted State Boards - **80% and above in English**. |
| WAEC | **C6 or above** |
As part of the application process, international students need to submit evidence of English Language proficiency, unless they’re a national of a [majority English speaking country](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/international/applying/entry-requirements/english-language-requirements/majority-english-speaking-countries/).
If you don’t meet the English language requirements, the University can use your most recent IELTS score, or [the equivalent score in selected other English language tests](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/english-language-centre/pre-sessional-english-courses/course-overview/entry-requirements/ielts-band-b#other-tests), to determine the length of Pre-sessional English course required.

Program Overview.content:
Qualification type: MSc. Study mode: full-time or part-time. Duration: 12 months full-time or 24 months part-time.
This course will enable you to develop a high level understanding of quantitative and computational geographical methods, including skills in GIS software and statistical programming languages such as R or Python. Within an applied setting, you will develop skills in the visualisation, modelling and statistical analysis of conventional and novel sources of data, ranging from censuses and social surveys through to satellite imagery and social media using both web-based and traditional techniques.
Human activity is increasingly associated with the generation of large volumes of data, including transactional data, administrative data, social media data shadows, and smart-card linked transport data. Many grand human challenges concern problems of a geographical nature, and growing volumes of big data about the form, function and dynamics of human activities are providing new opportunities to advance such debates within a framework of Geographic Data Science.
This MSc is also available with the alternative title Geographic Data Science MSc for entry September 2026, and gives students the option to graduate with either of these two MSc titles.
This course is for you if you want to understand and analyse the role of geography in everyday life through geographical and computational reasoning.
What you'll learn includes integrating the modern GIS toolkit with Data Science tools to solve practical real-world problems; applying GIS in the handling and analysis of spatial data in planning and social sciences; research methodology, philosophy, strategy and design; ethical and practical considerations associated with conducting research; social survey data analysis using descriptive and inferential statistics, data visualisation, regression modelling and model diagnostics; analytical techniques for spatial data; and major debates of society, environment, space and place.
The programme includes compulsory modules in Geographic Data Science that introduce the field where GIS and Data Science intersect, programming with Python, the importance of GDS for social science applications, GIS tools for creating digital representations of the world, qualitative research methods and research design, and social survey data analysis using R. In semester two, students learn statistical techniques for handling spatial data, current debates in the discipline, web-based map visualisation and analysis, and the importance of time and location in new forms of data. Optional modules allow study in areas such as Big Data problems, database systems and SQL, biologically inspired optimisation, population science theory, digital trace data analysis, and social and spatial inequalities. The final project includes an introductory dissertation seminar, progress sessions, and supervision sessions or pastoral tutorials with a dissertation supervisor to support development and completion of the dissertation.
You’ll learn through lectures, seminars, and hands-on workshops in the computer lab. Assessments are designed flexibly to provide student centred, research-led learning, and take the form of short (~3000 word) reports, computational essays, oral presentations, computer exercises, examinations and a 12,000 maximum word dissertation.
You will work with academic staff within the [Geographic Data Science Laboratory](http://www.geographicdatascience.com/) and the Centre for Spatial Demographic Research. You can also access the [Consumer Data Research Centre](http://cdrc.ac.uk/), created as part of a £6m investment in Big Data by the Economic and Social Research Council.
This program will give you the high-level skills you need to kickstart your career in applied geographical information science, data science with a geographic focus, or research with expertise in spatial analysis, GIS, and data science. Career options after graduation include PhD or postdoctoral research, GIS/Data Science consultant roles, employment in the commercial or public sector, IT consulting, or teaching in higher education. With the programming and web development skills you’ll gain, you’ll be in high demand in the job market for newer spatial data handling skills, which are more in demand than traditional GIS skills.

Curriculum.content:
Study mode: Full-time or part-time. Duration: 12 months or 24 months.
Course content is organised across semester one, semester two, and a final project. Programme details and modules listed are illustrative only and subject to change. No more than five modules can be taken in one semester.
Semester one: compulsory modules in Geographic Data Science (GDS) give a comprehensive introduction to the field where GIS and Data Science intersect, including programming with Python, GIS tools, qualitative research methods, research design, and social survey data analysis using R. Optional modules include Big Data problems, database systems and SQL.

Assessment takes the form of short (~3000 word) reports, computational essays, oral presentations, computer exercises, examinations and a **12,000 maximum word dissertation**.

Cost of Attendance.content:
UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) requires that you have **£10,539 per academic year**, equivalent to **£1,171 per month for nine months**. This is designed to cover daily living expenses and includes things like accommodation, food and local travel. The £10,539 figure is based on a nine-month stay in the UK. If staying for 12 months, you are likely to need at least **£14,052** to cover living costs, based on the UKVI's minimum monthly amount.
The University estimates total monthly living expenses of **£900-£1,350** based on feedback from current international undergraduate and master's students. Typical monthly costs include:
- University halls accommodation, including electricity, gas, water, and Wi-Fi: **£688-£1,120 per month**
- Private accommodation: **£400-£700 per month**
- Household bills for private accommodation, including electricity, gas, water, and Wi-Fi: **£50-£200 per month**
- Travel and transport: **£20-£80 per month**
- Food and other household necessities: **£150-£400 per month**
- Mobile phone bill: **£15-£50 per month**
- Television Licence: **£14.12 per month** or **£169.50 for the full year**
- Socialising and entertainment: **£50-£200 per month**
- Study costs, such as books and photocopying: **£10-£30 per month**
- Gym membership, based on University Sports Centre: **From £22 per month**

Financial Aid.content:
We offer a generous range of scholarships and bursaries for master's students. You can search the full list using our [scholarships finder](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/scholarships-and-bursaries/finder/?level=masters "Scholarships Finder").
- Liverpool Scholarships for 2026/2027, worth up to **£9,000**, are designed to support outstanding international students who demonstrate academic excellence.
- [Liverpool Excellence Scholarship for Postgraduates](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/scholarships-and-bursaries/masters/liverpool-excellence-scholarship-postgraduate/): International postgraduate students with a First Class or equivalent undergraduate degree could get a **£7,000 tuition fee discount**.
- [Liverpool Advancement Scholarship](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/scholarships-and-bursaries/masters/liverpool-advancement-scholarship): Students from Indonesia, Malaysia, Nigeria, Pakistan, South Korea, Thailand, Turkey or Vietnam may be eligible for a **£5,000 tuition fee discount**.
- [Liverpool Achievement Scholarship for India](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/scholarships-and-bursaries/masters/liverpool-achievement-scholarship-india): You could receive a **£5,000 tuition fee discount** if you're a postgraduate student from India, with a 2:1 or equivalent undergraduate degree.
- [Liverpool Attainment Scholarship for India](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/scholarships-and-bursaries/masters/liverpool-attainment-scholarship-india): Get a **£2,000 tuition fee discount** if you're a postgraduate student from India and meet the conditions of your offer.
- Liverpool Loyalty Scholarships offer substantial tuition fee discounts to University of Liverpool graduates who progress to postgraduate study.
- [Liverpool Excellence Scholarship for International Postgraduates](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/scholarships-and-bursaries/masters/liverpool-excellence-scholarship-postgraduate/): International postgraduate students who have studied at the University before, with a First Class or equivalent undergraduate degree, could get a **£7,000 tuition fee discount**.
- [Graduate Loyalty Scholarship - International students](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/scholarships-and-bursaries/masters/graduate-loyalty-scholarship-international/): International students who completed their undergraduate degree at the University of Liverpool could receive a **£5,000 tuition fee discount**.
- [Bracken Scholarship](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/scholarships-and-bursaries/masters/bracken-scholarship/): Studying a master's in any subject and aspiring to a career using data and digital skills in the public sector or within public missions? If you live in the Liverpool City Region, you could be eligible for this **£5,000 scholarship**.

Multiple Applications.content: Please note that you can accept only one unconditional offer. If you have been made unconditional offers for more than one programme, you will need to choose one to accept. The Admissions Team will then decline any other offers.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: If for an unforeseen reason you are not able to take up the place of an offer for the academic year you have applied for, you can defer your offer of a place for **one academic year**. You can only defer your studies once. If you request to defer your offer, and then ask to defer again the following year, the Admissions Team will not be able to process the request, and a new application will have to be submitted. You may only request a deferral up until **31 October** for the following year's entry. After this date a deferral may not be possible. To request a deferral for postgraduate taught programmes, please use the [postgraduate application tracker](https://pgapptracker.liverpool.ac.uk/).
